key_insight: You can extract reliable Q-value estimates from a behavior-cloned policy and use those estimates to gate online reinforcement learning updates, enabling safe, sample-efficient on-robot improvement without overwriting good demonstrated behaviors.
problem_solved: Behavior Cloning (BC) lacks a self-guided mechanism for online improvement and naive offline-to-online fine-tuning can overwrite high-quality demonstrated actions due to distribution mismatch.
method: Train a behavior-cloned policy from demonstrations and learn a critic to produce Q-value estimates for BC actions (Q-Estimation).
Use Q-Gating: allow online RL updates only when proposed updates improve estimated Q-values, blocking updates that would degrade BC-derived good actions.
Combine the gated updates with standard online RL to safely improve policy where demonstrations are suboptimal while preserving demonstrated behavior elsewhere.
impact: Enables robots to continue learning on-device safely and efficiently after demonstration collection, reducing catastrophic replacement of good behaviors and improving sample-efficiency for real-world deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Demonstrations → Behavior Cloning → Q-Estimation → Q-Gating → Online RL (highlight gated paths).
Before/After performance chart: naive fine-tuning vs Q2RL showing preservation of demonstrated success and improved areas.
Heatmap or bar overlay of Q-values across actions/states to show where gating permits vs blocks updates.
Robot-in-the-loop iconography showing safe on-robot adaptation (e.g., shield over preserved actions, upward arrow for learned improvements).
paper_title: When Life Gives You BC, Make Q-functions: Extracting Q-values from Behavior Cloning for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Lakshita Dodeja, Ondrej Biza, Shivam Vats, Stephen Hart, Stefanie Tellex
